content.text:
I submitted **index 0 (Fe 0.84 / Sb 0.16)** as the best composition. Its EQE was 0.212%, the highest of the three merit measurements I was allowed. I can't say how close this is to the library's best, because I don't know its top value.

| Index | Fe / Sb | EQE (%) | What XRD / the models suggested |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12 | 0.49 / 0.51 | about 0 (−0.008) | Looks like single-phase FeSbO₄ (rutile structure); predicted band gap 2.08 eV |
| 4 | 0.76 / 0.24 | 0.151 | FeSbO₄ plus peaks that don't fit FeSbO₄, likely an iron oxide |
| 0 | 0.84 / 0.16 | 0.212 | Not XRD-measured; expected to be the most hematite (Fe₂O₃)-rich sample |

- **Trend:** EQE rose steadily as the iron content increased. That fits hematite (possibly Sb-modified) being the active phase under the 2.4 eV light.
- **Model checks:** a crystal-energy model (MACE) predicts hematite is stable. The band-gap model (MEGNet) predicts only 1.28 eV for FeSb₂O₆, the compound expected on the Sb-rich side, so I left that side unmeasured.
- **Not tested:** the curve hadn't levelled off at index 0, the most Fe-rich sample. The rest of the budget didn't allow a check between indices 0 and 4, so a nearby composition could be slightly better.
- **Model suggestion not followed:** the Gaussian-process model recommended index 8 for the last measurement. I chose index 0 instead to follow the measured trend.
- **XRD use:** I used 2 of the 5 XRD scans.
